mission: HEADROOM PHASE-4 - VERIFICATION-AWARE RUNTIME GATE, MIGRATION STEP 4: STRICT VERIFIED EXECUTION BOUNDARY (no UI, no Phase 4E)
phase4RuntimeTreeAtEnd: unchanged - the boundary sits beside the runtime, not inside it

boundary.whyBesideNotInsideTheRuntime: the runtime may not import the compiler (pinned by tests/contract-model/runtime/anti-enumeration.test.ts); the certified resolver is an adapter that imports compiler TYPES; the boundary needs the resolver, so it lives as a sibling of runtime/ and verification-envelope/, and imports the compiler type-only.
boundary.invariant: Headroom executes legal capacity or transaction logic in product mode only from IR that has a corresponding verification artifact, under policy REQUIRE.
boundary.policy: VERIFIED_EXECUTION_POLICY = "REQUIRE" as const - a constant, not an argument. VerifiedCapacityArgs has no policy field (a @ts-expect-error test pins it); a smuggled field is ignored at runtime (pinned); the boundary source never names ALLOW_MISSING in code (pinned).
boundary.notAGenericWrapper: the names say verified; the results say policy: REQUIRE; the only way to get a CapacityState or a TransactionSimulationResult out is through the package binding below.

inputPackage.type: VerifiedExecutionPackage { companyId; instrumentKey; rules; definitions?; sharedCapacities?; verifications: VerifiedUnitArtifact[] }
inputPackage.artifact: VerifiedUnitArtifact { ruleOrDefinitionId; kind: RULE|DEFINITION; verifiedIdentity: RuntimeVerificationIdentity; result: SemanticVerificationResult }
inputPackage.noPreLabelledBoolean: there is no `verified: true` anywhere. Safety is derived from the artifacts: the result (verbatim, never mutated) plus the identity of the IR the verifier saw.
inputPackage.whyVerifiedIdentityIsInThePackage: SemanticVerificationResult carries no IR version identity (no irSchemaVersion / compilerVersion / sourceContentVersion). The resolver derives identity from the IR unit in hand, which can only ever match itself. So the Phase-3 run that produced both must persist the identity of the IR it verified; that claim is what the gate checks against the IR actually executed, and a stale pairing fails closed. This is the small paired-persistence type §20 asked for - designed here, no storage migration attempted.
inputPackage.capacityArgs: VerifiedCapacityArgs { package; inputs: InputResolver (Phase-4B snapshot resolver); ledger?; ledgerPolicy?; asOf? }
inputPackage.transactionArgs: VerifiedTransactionArgs extends VerifiedCapacityArgs { transaction; selectedPath } - no state, no graph; the pre-state is produced inside by the verified capacity path from the same package (pinned by a source-shape test).

envelopeConstruction.where: inside evaluateVerifiedCapacity, immediately before buildCapacityGraph / evaluateCapacityState, through resolveRuntimeVerificationEnvelope over the exact IR units being executed
envelopeConstruction.identityHandling: the resolver resolves paths -> exprIds against the unit in hand (what it needs), then each record's identity is REPLACED by the artifact's verifiedIdentity (the verifier's claim) with strength recomputed. The gate then compares claim against the executed IR's identity and fails closed on any disagreement. No new comparison logic; the certified step-3 check does the work.
envelopeConstruction.neverSynthesized: zero artifacts -> REFUSED VERIFICATION_ARTIFACT_INCOMPLETE, not an empty envelope

refusalVocabulary.VERIFICATION_ARTIFACT_INCOMPLETE: no verification artifact supplied at all
refusalVocabulary.VERIFICATION_IDENTITY_UNBOUND: an artifact names a unit the package does not carry, names the wrong kind, contradicts its own identity claim, or two artifacts claim one unit
refusalVocabulary.IR_PACKAGE_INCONSISTENT: a unit belongs to another company/instrument than the package states, or a unit id appears twice
refusalVocabulary.everythingElse: flows through the step-3 gate inside the runtime: REQUIRED_VERIFICATION_MISSING / IDENTITY_MISMATCH / MATERIAL_UNIT_FINDING / MATERIAL_NODE_HIT / ATTEMPTED_INCOMPLETE, as limitations on the capacity entries and on the simulation
refusalVocabulary.whenRefusedVsExecuted: REFUSED only when the package is structurally unusable (the three codes above); nothing is evaluated then. Partial coverage EXECUTES: uncovered units fail closed inside the runtime under REQUIRE, verified units stay independently readable (§15), and the coverage report names every missing, refused and incompletely verified unit with complete=false.

coverageReport: VerificationCoverage { unitsInPackage; unitsWithVerification; unitsMissingVerification[]; unitsRefusedByGate[{unitId, reason, identityStrength}]; unitsIncompletelyVerified[]; identityStrength {STRONG, WEAK}; verificationStatuses; complete } - `complete` is coverage completeness (every executed unit has a matched, completed record), never a 'clean' claim; a WEAK match counts under WEAK and no 'verified-clean' field exists.
noReVerification: imports the compiler type-only (pinned); no fetch, no getStageCaller, no verify import, no process.env, no filesystem, no prisma (pinned by comment-stripped scan); artifacts byte-identical after execution (pinned).

matrix.A_CLEAN: STRONG-identity rule MUL(PCT(0.2), FIGURE fig-1=1000) with artifact -> AVAILABLE, effectiveRemaining 200, no limitation; coverage complete; the CapacityState is BYTE-IDENTICAL (stateHash and JSON) to the raw ALLOW_MISSING evaluation with no envelope - REQUIRE degrades nothing clean
matrix.B_MISSING_VERIFICATION: verifications [] -> REFUSED [VERIFICATION_ARTIFACT_INCOMPLETE], no state, packageHash still reported
matrix.C_MISSING_UNIT: rules A,B with artifact for A -> EXECUTED; A AVAILABLE 200; B REVIEW_REQUIRED [REQUIRED_VERIFICATION_MISSING], gross NOT_DETERMINED; coverage.unitsMissingVerification [B], unitsRefusedByGate [B REQUIRED_VERIFICATION_MISSING], complete false
matrix.D_TRANSITIVE_MISSING: A -> definition EBITDA with artifact for A only -> A REVIEW_REQUIRED with [REQUIRED_VERIFICATION_MISSING] naming d-ebitda; both artifacts -> AVAILABLE 200, complete true. Same for A -> RULE_REFERENCE C (REVIEW_REQUIRED naming p-c; both -> AVAILABLE 500)
matrix.E_MATERIAL_NODE: finding on the PERCENT literal -> UNSUPPORTED [MATERIAL_NODE_HIT], gross NOT_DETERMINED, 200 absent; not a unit refusal
matrix.G_IDENTITY_MISMATCH: artifact claims compilerVersion c-old vs c1 -> REVIEW_REQUIRED [IDENTITY_MISMATCH … compilerVersion]; coverage refused IDENTITY_MISMATCH, complete false; a NODE finding on a stale (irSchemaVersion) record is not salvaged
matrix.H_INCOMPLETE: VERIFICATION_INCOMPLETE / VERIFICATION_FAILED / NOT_VERIFIED with no finding -> REVIEW_REQUIRED under PHASE3_VERIFICATION_INCOMPLETE only, provisional 200, coverage.unitsIncompletelyVerified; incomplete + a NODE finding -> UNSUPPORTED with both codes (the finding still blocks by scope)
matrix.I_CLEAN_TRANSACTION: consume 20 of 200 -> SATISFIED / SIMULATED / committable true; the simulation is BYTE-IDENTICAL to simulateTransaction over the raw world
matrix.J_BLOCKED_TRANSACTION: capacity UNSUPPORTED by a NODE finding -> selectedPathResult REVIEW_REQUIRED, simulationStatus REVIEW_REQUIRED, PHASE3_VERIFICATION_MATERIAL_FINDING, committable false; package and ledger byte-identical afterwards; preTransactionState.stateHash equals the verified state's; 200 never surfaced
matrix.K_WRONG_COMPANY: artifact claiming another companyId -> [IDENTITY_MISMATCH … companyId] fail closed; an IR unit for another company -> REFUSED [IR_PACKAGE_INCONSISTENT refs p-foreign]
matrix.M_WEAK_IDENTITY: null/null source version -> executes AVAILABLE, identityStrength {STRONG 0, WEAK 1}, no verifiedClean/VERIFIED_CLEAN/verified:true anywhere; a claimed s1 the IR does not carry -> [IDENTITY_MISMATCH … sourceContentVersion]; a finding on the WEAK record -> UNSUPPORTED
matrix.N_BYPASS: architecture test: every non-test .ts/.tsx under app/, components/, lib/ - except lib/contract-model/runtime/**, lib/contract-model/verification-envelope/** and the boundary itself - may not import any specifier matching contract-model/runtime(/|$). Offenders today: []. The rule is proven live (the boundary itself imports capacity/state, transaction/simulate and the resolver) and covers the bare barrel path (which re-exports the 4A primitives).

chainIntegrity.10B_ruleAvsRuleB: artifact for A with package [B] -> REFUSED [VERIFICATION_IDENTITY_UNBOUND refs p-a]; an artifact whose verifiedIdentity names another unit, or the wrong kind, is unbound
chainIntegrity.noObjectReferenceIdentity: binding is by ruleOrDefinitionId + the version trio + company/instrument; the envelope's units are exactly the artifacts' units carrying the verifier's claim (pinned)
chainIntegrity.packageHash: sha256 over company, instrument, rules, definitions, shared capacities and each artifact's (id, kind, identity, status, findings, verifierAlgorithmVersion, evidenceSetHash); deterministic; a changed verification is a different package (pinned)
